hostgen.asm_signatures_why: func_0038B448 (PAL func_0038B500, the turned glyph quad host/ui2d.c wraps), run from the disc on both discs since its VU0 helpers are inline assembly Clang cannot read: the wrapper's prototype, with its colour and texture words signed. FontPrint (PAL's func_0038EBC8): host/ui2d.c wraps it as a void function, as PAL's prototype has it; NTSC-U's assembly leaves $v0 as a callee's, which hostgen took for a result; the follow camera's stick read (PAL's func_L01_003E92F8, whose C gives PAL its prototype): host/camera_latch.c wraps it with the camera and the two axes' addresses, NTSC-U's copy being assembly here After the rac3-decomp 4e0324fd bump: 93 NTSC-U functions translated from the disc whose newly matched PAL C (status differs here) declared fewer argument registers, or a callee's int result where its caller reads $f0 (or $v0 of a void one): each takes the registers its code reads (hostgen's signature check, the extra ones after the declared parameters) and the result its callers read.
hostgen.places_why: NTSC-U's own level catalogue, in its own names: every level function is translated from the disc's level programs (no src/levels C yet: its names and its levels' data are PAL's)
hostgen.call_copies_why: rac3-pal's table (call_copies_rac3.py) holds PAL's places; NTSC-U's catalogue has its own, to be written the same way
hostgen.split_places_why: NTSC-U's own tables/split_places.tsv: the multiplayer maps' copies of the font width wrapper (func_L01_00410820) are their own function, func_L39_005187A0, whose name the carry leaves out as no function of NTSC-U's catalogue; its signature below, as rac3-pal's func_L39_005189A0
hostgen.more_places_why: rac3-pal's are PAL's places: on the Phoenix (03) and in the Insomniac Museum (24) the catalogue folds the Vid-comic password panel's byte getter and clear into func_L01_004C78E0 and func_L01_004D75F8 and func_L01_004C78E0's real twin into func_L01_004D4C50 (tables/split_places.tsv splits them off); in Holostar Studios as Clank (23) it folds the help box's flag setter's real twin into func_L01_004D4B48 and another flag's setter into func_L01_004C78D8; and in the 24 story levels outside Veldin's family it files nine class type getters one row along (tables/split_places.tsv), the loading flight's destination getter func_L01_004D2120 among them; the real twins at NTSC-U's places; and where a caller's own code reaches a class getter or the draw callback adder (func_L01_003EE980, func_L01_004026A0, func_L01_004D4B48) at a place the catalogue files under another row, the real copy (found from the callers' calls at the same instruction)
hostgen.roots_why: func_003932B0__frontbin: NTSC-U's twin of PAL's func_00397B10 (one constant changed, so map.tsv has no pair), whose address func_00391E78 stores; reached only through it.
hostgen.from_assembly_why: func_00387778 (the clip view, PAL func_003877A0), func_003AD9F0 (PAL func_003ADB90), func_003C0160 (PAL func_003C0268): map.tsv's match, but their C reads globals and calls functions config/us/names.tsv places for the front end or not at all (func_00387778's D_001D9A10, D_00334F00 to D_00335D50 and func_0027AB40; func_003C0160's D_001DA348 to D_001DA390 aliases, all moved by +0x30 or +0x80 on NTSC-U), so hostgen made each a stub that does nothing. func_00391E78__frontbin (PAL func_003966D8) stores the address of PAL's func_00397B10, which NTSC-U has as 0x003932B0 with one constant changed (5, not 4). Run from the disc's instructions instead. func_003BE710 (PAL func_003BE800, the level loader's state that levels 27 and 28 run through the table at 0x0031C910): map.tsv's match since rac3-decomp 45baf7e5, but its C reads the per-caller aliases D_001D8D28_003BE800 to D_001DA2D0_003BE800g, which config/us/names.tsv gives no boot_elf value, so hostgen made it a stub that does nothing (before, NTSC-U ran it from assembly as a twin of a left-out definition).

front_globals.about: NTSC-U's value of a global of the front end (frontbin, a program of its own) that the C of a match function of frontbin reads and config/us/names.tsv gives a boot_elf row only for (release_rac3.py): PAL's name, NTSC-U's address in frontbin, the evidence. The boot program's row is another datum: frontbin's .text starts at 0x0037D100 on NTSC-U (README.md), PAL's at 0x00381080 as the boot program's.

D_0037FBE0.why: func_003BD030 (NTSC-U func_003B7B50, match), the scene switch's callbacks (value, init, step, event, render, finish; 24 bytes a row): its instruction 0x1C0 is addiu -0x420 on lui 0x0038 (0x0037FBE0) on PAL, addiu -0x43D0 (0x0037BC30) on NTSC-U, in frontbin as loaded (RAM dumps of both discs); frontbin's 1,778 comparable twins of map.tsv reach it so with no other vote, and its neighbours D_0037FA64 (0x0037BAB4) and D_0037FFE8 (0x0037C038) in names.tsv move the same -0x3FB0. The boot program's 0x0037FC70 is frontbin's code there: its row 8 read the words 0x7FA300C0, 0x27B000D0, 0x27A500A0 and 0x0C0EFCBE as init, step, event and render, and New Game from frontbin never left the loading screen

D_0037FCB8.why: func_003BD030 (NTSC-U func_003B7B50, match), the scene switch's rules (from, to, row, two arguments; 16 bytes each): its instruction 0x114 is addiu -0x348 on lui 0x0038 (0x0037FCB8) on PAL, addiu -0x42F8 (0x0037BD08) on NTSC-U, in frontbin as loaded; the twins reach it so with no other vote, the same -0x3FB0 as D_0037FBE0. At the boot program's 0x0037FD48, frontbin's code, no rule matched and the switch took the default row 8

mp_hostgen.about: Keys over rac3-pal's carried mp/hostgen.json (the multiplayer executable, I5BOOTN.ELF).
mp_hostgen.title: Ratchet & Clank: Up Your Arsenal (NTSC-U), multiplayer
mp_hostgen.gp_why: NTSC-U's level 39 $gp (config/gp.tsv), the program the executable runs its menus in, as PAL's 0x00247FC0 is both
mp_hostgen.host_why: the shared host C (rac3-pal's), read through rac3-ntsc's host/rac3_names.tsv, as the NTSC-U program's own
mp_hostgen.relocate_why: the programs' range from level 39's .lit, NTSC-U's 0x00241B80 (its level ELF; PAL's .lit starts at 0x00241A00, the boot program's rule: the first loaded program's .lit), up to 0x00700000 as PAL's

mp_addresses.about: NTSC-U's address of a multiplayer executable global the host C writes as RAC3_MADDR(address) that rac3_mp_pairs.py does not pair: PAL's address, NTSC-U's, why.

0x00241458.why: the two font headers: the multiplayer core's FontUpload and FontSelect (PAL mp_func_00280B18 / mp_func_00280D98) and level 39's and the maps' FontSelect copies (PAL mp_func_L39_00591BA0, NTSC-U mp_func_L40_0045DC68 among others) read and write it; NTSC-U's translation has it 0x180 on, as the core's other globals there (0x002412DC, 0x00241A00) (NTSC-U adds 0x15D8 to 0x00240000)

0x00241470.why: the font FontSelect chose last: the multiplayer core's FontUpload and FontSelect (PAL mp_func_00280B18 / mp_func_00280D98) and level 39's and the maps' FontSelect copies (PAL mp_func_L39_00591BA0, NTSC-U mp_func_L40_0045DC68 among others) read and write it; NTSC-U's translation has it 0x180 on, as the core's other globals there (0x002412DC, 0x00241A00) (NTSC-U's map copies store it at 0x002415F0)

0x00241CE8.why: the core's pointer to the current font's page handles: the multiplayer core's FontUpload and FontSelect (PAL mp_func_00280B18 / mp_func_00280D98) and level 39's and the maps' FontSelect copies (PAL mp_func_L39_00591BA0, NTSC-U mp_func_L40_0045DC68 among others) read and write it; NTSC-U's translation has it 0x180 on, as the core's other globals there (0x002412DC, 0x00241A00) (NTSC-U reads 0x00241E68 beside 0x00241E6C)

0x00241CEC.why: the core's pointer to the current font's palette handles, beside 0x00241CE8: the multiplayer core's FontUpload and FontSelect (PAL mp_func_00280B18 / mp_func_00280D98) and level 39's and the maps' FontSelect copies (PAL mp_func_L39_00591BA0, NTSC-U mp_func_L40_0045DC68 among others) read and write it; NTSC-U's translation has it 0x180 on, as the core's other globals there (0x002412DC, 0x00241A00)

0x00242820.why: level 39's (and the maps') pointer to the current font's page handles: the multiplayer core's FontUpload and FontSelect (PAL mp_func_00280B18 / mp_func_00280D98) and level 39's and the maps' FontSelect copies (PAL mp_func_L39_00591BA0, NTSC-U mp_func_L40_0045DC68 among others) read and write it; NTSC-U's translation has it 0x180 on, as the core's other globals there (0x002412DC, 0x00241A00) (NTSC-U's map copies store 0x002429A0)

0x00242824.why: level 39's (and the maps') pointer to the palette handles, beside 0x00242820: the multiplayer core's FontUpload and FontSelect (PAL mp_func_00280B18 / mp_func_00280D98) and level 39's and the maps' FontSelect copies (PAL mp_func_L39_00591BA0, NTSC-U mp_func_L40_0045DC68 among others) read and write it; NTSC-U's translation has it 0x180 on, as the core's other globals there (0x002412DC, 0x00241A00)

0x00230000.why: the screen whose size (+0x150, +0x152) SetScissor keeps its rectangle within: PAL mp_func_00299218 and NTSC-U mp_func_002991F8, the same instructions, both read 0x00230150 and 0x00230152

0x002412DC.why: the level whose program is loaded: read at $gp - 0x6CE4 in both cores (PAL 0x00199150, 0x002945BC, 0x00295534 with $gp 0x00247FC0; NTSC-U 0x00199290, 0x00295524 with $gp 0x00248140)
